semantically_equivalent_domains.justification: While immunology is a broader field, t-cell biology is a subfield of immunology, showing significant overlap and semantic equivalence in the context of where T-cells are the primary focus.

parent_domains.justification: Immunology is the study of the immune system as a whole, of which t-cells are a critical component. Therefore, immunology serves as a parent domain to t-cell biology.

Biology is a broad science that covers all living organisms and their vital processes. Since t-cell biology studies a particular aspect of living organisms, it falls under the broad umbrella of biology.

closest_parent_domain.justification: Immunology is much more closely related to t-cell biology than the broader biology category, as t-cell biology specifically involves the immune system, of which immunology is the dedicated study.

child_domains.justification: Cell biology deals with the fundamental organizational unit of life, providing a foundational understanding of t-cells but does not focus on their immunological roles.
T-cell biology is a specific study within the immune system, making immune system studies a more general domain that could encompass t-cell research.

closest_child_domain.justification: While both cell biology and immune system studies are relevant, immune system studies focuses more specifically on the components and functions of the immune system, aligning more closely with t-cell biology.

sibling_domains.justification: Although this domain can also be seen as a child domain, when considering immunology as the parent, immune system studies becomes a sibling as they both fall directly under immunology.

Immunoinformatics focuses on computational methods and tools for understanding immunology and the immune system, and since t-cell biology relies on some of the same data and tools, it is considered a sibling domain.
This domain focuses on treatments involving immune cells like t-cells, making it a sibling, though more application-focused than biological.

closest_sibling_domain.justification: Cellular immunotherapy closely relates to t-cell biology as it deals with the application of knowledge about t-cells and other immune cells to develop treatments.

unrelated_domains.justification: This domain is related to the study and analysis techniques for individual cells. However, it doesn’t specifically focus on T-cells or immune-related cells, making it unrelated to direct t-cell biology research.
Similar to single-cell analysis, this domain deals with data science methodologies for handling single-cell data across different biological fields, but without specific emphasis on T-cells.
This domain focuses on the genomics of single cells and would only intersect with t-cell biology if specifically applied; thus, it's generally unrelated.
Like the other single-cell domains, this focuses on sequencing technologies for single-cell studies, without specific focus on T-cells.
This domain involves RNA sequencing at the single-cell level, which does not inherently focus on immune functions or T-cells.
This domain is unrelated as it doesn't have any explicit ties to biological or cellular processes.
While membrane biology can be tangentially related as cellular membranes are important in immune cell function, it doesn't focus on T-cells or immune specifics.
Data simulation at the single-cell RNA sequencing level; though potentially useful for T-cell studies, it is not inherently related to T-cell biology.
Involves transcriptomics at the single-cell level, is not specifically about immune cells or T-cells.
Broad domain focused on computational methods; while potentially applicable to T-cell biology, it is not inherently specific to it.
Focuses on complex interactions within biological systems and is broader in scope than T-cell biology.
This domain deals with biological activity at a molecular level and, while relevant to T-cell research, does not focus specifically on T-cells.
Similar to single-cell RNA-seq and other single-cell domains, this area does not specifically involve T-cell biology.
Studies the molecular structure of biological macromolecules which can intersect with T-cell biology but is not inherently focused on T-cells.
